results.name: network_session_find_machine_by_id
results.evidence: Loops 16 times over a 0x60-byte-stride table at (esi+0x3c4)+i*0x60 comparing a short id field to unaff_EDI and returning the slot base (esi+0x3b8+i*0x60) or 0.
results.summary: Searches the session's 16-entry machine table for a slot whose id field matches the given machine id and returns a pointer to that slot, or NULL if not found.

results.name: network_session_validate_client_version
results.evidence: Compares a version/build value read from DAT_0087bc1c[DAT_006f16d0] against thresholds 0x9663f/0x96640 and a channel flag before scanning the 16-slot machine table for a free entry (id==-1), returning distinct integer status codes 0/4/5/6/7.
results.summary: Validates a connecting client's build/version and channel state against accepted ranges and returns a numeric status/error code, checking for a free machine slot on success.

results.name: network_join_password_is_set
results.evidence: Calls _wcsncmp against an empty wide string on the 8-wchar field at object+0x9fc, the same storage location written by FUN_004e0910 and read by FUN_004e0930.
results.summary: Returns true if the session's wide-character password field at offset 0x9fc is non-empty.

results.name: network_join_set_password
results.evidence: _wcsncpy's the input wide string into (esi+0x9fc), max 8 chars, and null-terminates the field at +0xa0c; called from sv_password after updating the stored password.
results.summary: Copies up to 8 wide characters into the connection/session object's password field at offset 0x9fc.

results.name: network_join_get_password
results.evidence: _wcsncpy's from (eax+0x9fc) into the caller's buffer and null-terminates it -- the inverse of FUN_004e0910, used during join/password comparisons in FUN_004e21d0.
results.summary: Copies the session's stored password (offset 0x9fc) out into the caller-supplied wide-character buffer.

results.name: network_game_send_short_info_reply
results.evidence: Copies a 7-char short name (from FUN_00575fa0) plus a 0x84-byte game-data blob and a flag byte into a buffer, encodes it as message type 4 via data_packet_group_encode_packet, then writes the resulting bytes straight into a channel's send buffer via FUN_004cf8f0.
results.summary: Builds and queues a small 'game info' style packet (short name plus a game-data snapshot) for the channel referenced by param_2, encoded as message type 4.

results.name: network_channel_teardown_helper
results.evidence: Trivial two-call wrapper (FUN_004dd390(); FUN_00575ff0();) invoked from the password/join-check path in FUN_004e21d0 with no parameters shown in this decompilation.
results.summary: Calls two parameterless helper routines, likely resetting some channel/session state as part of the join-request handshake.

results.name: network_game_send_challenge_or_retry
results.evidence: If the target machine's channel exists and its 0xa98 flag is set it marks DAT_0071c2de and calls FUN_004aa900(); otherwise it builds a packet via network_prepare_challenge_packet and unicasts it with FUN_004e1930, then always schedules a retry via FUN_004df090(1000).
results.summary: Either notifies that a machine's connection is already established or (re)sends a prepared challenge/info packet to it and arms a 1000ms retry.

results.name: network_session_find_and_reset_machine
results.evidence: Same 16-slot machine-table search pattern as FUN_004e0810, but additionally clears a byte at slot+0x50 when a match is found.
results.summary: Finds the machine-table slot matching a given id and clears a flag/name byte at offset 0x50 within that slot.

results.name: network_game_send_full_info_reply
results.evidence: Encodes a 1536-byte buffer as message type 7 via data_packet_group_encode_packet (compare to type 4 in FUN_004e0950), then queues the bytes into the channel's send buffer via FUN_004cf8f0/FUN_004ddb60 and sets flag bit 0x10 on param_1.
results.summary: Builds and queues a larger 'full game info' packet (message type 7) for a connecting machine, marking the request as answered.

results.name: network_channel_get_player_team
results.evidence: Validates a short index at object+0xc against table &DAT_006b1460, then calls datum_get() and returns the byte at offset 0x67 of the resulting datum, an offset also used by the player-iteration helper FUN_004e2c10.
results.summary: Looks up the player datum referenced by the object's stored index and returns a byte field (likely team or slot id) from it, or -1 if unavailable.

results.name: network_session_find_free_machine_slot
results.evidence: Requires a channel flag bit before scanning the 16-slot machine id table for the first free entry (id==-1); if a non-null param_2 is supplied it also calls network_channel_get_remote_address.
results.summary: Counts occupied machine-table slots up to the first free one and, for a new connection, fetches its remote address via network_channel_get_remote_address.

results.name: network_session_handle_machine_timeout
results.evidence: Uses QueryPerformanceCounter/__alldiv to get elapsed ms, compares to a version-range window on param_2, and on timeout unlinks/clears a machine-table slot (fields at +0x3b8.. +0x414), calls FUN_0061b3f0/FUN_0061b350 list bookkeeping, then posts an event via FUN_004ec940(0,0x21,...) and broadcasts DAT_00871de0 via FUN_004e19c0.
results.summary: Per-machine per-tick check that detects a stale/timed-out connection, tears down its machine-table slot, and broadcasts a player-left style notification.

results.name: network_session_update_machines
results.evidence: Iterates all 16 machine-table entries; for ones not yet connected (piVar5[4]==0) it drives FUN_004e1290's bitstream processing or retries via FUN_004df090(0), and for connected ones it calls FUN_004e0ef0 (timeout check) each pass.
results.summary: Per-frame pass over the session's 16 machine slots that advances pending connections and checks established ones for timeout.

results.name: network_session_process_machine_bitstream
results.evidence: Repeatedly reads single bits out of a shared bit-buffer (&DAT_00861de0) via FUN_004dcf10 and calls FUN_004e18b0(param_1, bit) for each bit until the buffer's bounds are exhausted.
results.summary: Drains a shared bitstream buffer one bit at a time, dispatching each bit through FUN_004e18b0 as part of connecting a new machine.

results.name: network_game_send_periodic_challenge
results.evidence: Computes elapsed ms via QueryPerformanceCounter/__alldiv and, once 5000ms have passed since (esi+0x9bc), builds a packet with network_prepare_challenge_packet and unicasts it via FUN_004e19c0, updating the stored timestamp.
results.summary: Resends a prepared challenge/info packet to a peer roughly every 5 seconds while a connection attempt is outstanding.

results.name: network_session_has_unestablished_machine
results.evidence: Scans the 16 machine-id slots for one whose id is within 0..15 and does not have bit 3 of its flag byte set, returning 0 if found and 1 if the whole table was scanned without a hit.
results.summary: Reports whether any machine slot is still awaiting a particular connection flag, used to gate further handshake work.

results.name: network_session_periodic_status_report
results.evidence: When channel flag bit 2 (param_1+6) is set and more than 15000ms have elapsed since DAT_0071c2f0 (computed via QueryPerformanceCounter/__alldiv), it calls sv_status() and updates the timestamp.
results.summary: Periodically (every ~15s) prints the dedicated server status by invoking sv_status when the relevant channel flag is active.

results.name: network_session_tick
results.evidence: Computes elapsed time, walks the 16-slot machine table posting disconnects for unestablished channels, and drives a multi-stage handshake (FUN_004e04f0/FUN_004e0480/FUN_004deb50/network_prepare_challenge_packet/FUN_004e19c0) with separate 5s and 60s timers.
results.summary: Main per-frame networking heartbeat that times out unestablished machines and advances the connection/challenge handshake state machine.

results.name: network_session_reset_to_defaults
results.evidence: Copies a 0x98-byte default block from DAT_0087aa80 and a default name string from DAT_0087aa40 into fields of the session object, clears several counters, and sets flag bits at offset 6 and on the underlying object at +0xae0.
results.summary: Resets a session/game-info object's name and data fields back to compiled-in defaults and marks it initialized.

results.name: network_session_count_active_machines
results.evidence: Loops the 16 machine-table entries, incrementing a counter for every slot whose base pointer field is non-null and whose id field is not -1.
results.summary: Counts how many of the session's 16 machine-table slots currently hold a valid, connected machine.

results.name: network_channel_dispatch_event
results.evidence: Branches on param_2: 1 calls FUN_004e1f40 (drain queued application messages), 0 first checks stack headroom via FUN_004de420(0xfff) then calls FUN_004e1c60 (decode an incoming network game message).
results.summary: Small dispatcher used while draining a channel's bitstream, routing each unit to either the queued-message processor or the incoming-packet decoder.

results.name: network_session_send_to_machine
results.evidence: Finds the machine-table slot matching an id (same search pattern as FUN_004e0810), confirms its channel isn't disconnecting unless overridden by param_6, then forwards to FUN_004dce40 to actually transmit.
results.summary: Sends a prepared packet to the single machine identified by id, skipping machines that are in the process of disconnecting.

results.name: network_session_broadcast_to_established
results.evidence: Iterates all 16 machine-table entries and calls FUN_004dce40 for each whose flag bit 1 is set (established) and whose channel is not marked disconnecting.
results.summary: Broadcasts a prepared packet to every established machine in the session's machine table.

results.name: network_session_broadcast_to_flagged
results.evidence: Nearly identical to FUN_004e19c0 but additionally requires flag bit 2 to be set on each machine-table entry before calling FUN_004dce40.
results.summary: Broadcasts a prepared packet only to machines whose table entry has an extra qualifying flag bit set, on top of being established.

results.name: network_game_broadcast_state_snapshot
results.evidence: Copies 8 dwords (32 bytes) from the caller's structure, encodes them as message type 0x17 via data_packet_group_encode_packet, and broadcasts the result through FUN_004e19c0.
results.summary: Packages a small fixed-size game-state structure into message type 0x17 and broadcasts it to all established machines.

results.name: network_session_broadcast_player_count_update
results.evidence: Calls FUN_004ec940(0,0x21,0,&param_1,0,1,0) to post an event referencing param_1, then on success broadcasts DAT_00871de0 to all established machines via FUN_004e19c0(1,...); invoked from multiple message handlers and from the machine-timeout path.
results.summary: Posts a type-0x21 game-engine event and, if accepted, broadcasts an associated update packet to the whole session -- used whenever the connected-player set changes.

results.name: network_game_process_incoming_message
results.evidence: Switches on a message-type byte extracted from the packet header and, for most cases, first calls data_packet_group_decode_packet against &PTR_s_network_game_messages_group_006994f8 before dispatching to a per-type handler (FUN_004e21d0, FUN_004e2400, ... FUN_004e2930).
results.summary: Top-level decoder/dispatcher for incoming 'network game' protocol messages, decoding each message with the network-game message group and routing it by type byte.

results.name: network_client_process_queued_messages
results.evidence: Loops calling FUN_004ec510 to dequeue an application message and, when present, dispatches on its type field to network_game_client_apply_received_update (0xd), FUN_004aabd0 (0xf), FUN_00470810 (0x1a), FUN_004e20b0 (0x34), FUN_004e4f00 (0x36).
results.summary: Drains the client's queued network-game update messages, applying each one according to its message-type tag.

results.name: network_client_record_player_elapsed_time
results.evidence: If the message's embedded pointer field is already set it calls FUN_004ec670; otherwise, after FUN_004ec590 succeeds it fetches the local player's datum via datum_get and stores (FUN_00449210() - stored_time) into datum+0xdc, an offset also read by the sv_players scoreboard code.
results.summary: Handles queued message type 0x34 by recording elapsed time since a stored timestamp into a field of the local player's datum.

results.name: network_game_send_timed_ack
results.evidence: Computes elapsed ms via QueryPerformanceCounter/__alldiv, builds a packet via network_prepare_challenge_packet, and if the target channel is not disconnecting sends it through FUN_004dcdb0 with a timestamp payload.
results.summary: Handles message type 1 by building and sending a timestamped acknowledgement/challenge packet back to the sender's channel.

results.name: network_message_handle_join_request
results.evidence: Decodes group-3 data, compares the incoming password (via FUN_004e0930/_wcsncmp) against the stored session password, then on success calls FUN_004e1bf0, sets a team/flag byte from DAT_006894a2, and unicasts a reply built from network_prepare_challenge_packet via FUN_004e1930.
results.summary: Handles message type 0xe: validates a client's join password and, if accepted, admits the machine and replies with a challenge/accept packet.

results.name: network_message_handle_join_confirm
results.evidence: Decodes group-3 data, and on FUN_004df840 failure re-sends via FUN_004e0af0, or on success calls FUN_004e1bf0 (player-count update) and unicasts a reply via network_prepare_challenge_packet/FUN_004e1930.
results.summary: Handles message type 0xf, the next step of the join handshake after FUN_004e21d0, finalizing or retrying the connection.

results.name: network_message_handle_0x10
results.evidence: Requires role field == 0, decodes a group-3 packet, and forwards the result to FUN_004df0e0.
results.summary: Server-side handler for message type 0x10 that decodes its payload and passes it to FUN_004df0e0.

results.name: network_message_handle_0x11
results.evidence: Requires role field 0 or 1, decodes a group-3 packet with no payload extracted, and on success calls FUN_004e1bf0 (player-count/broadcast update).
results.summary: Handles message type 0x11 by decoding it and triggering a session-wide player-count broadcast.

results.name: network_message_handle_0x12
results.evidence: Requires role field == 0, decodes a group-3 packet, then only if FUN_004de5f0 approves does it call FUN_004e1bf0.
results.summary: Handles message type 0x12, conditionally triggering a player-count broadcast after an approval check.

results.name: network_message_handle_0x13
results.evidence: Requires role field == 0, decodes a group-3 packet, then calls FUN_004e0590 with no further parameters shown.
results.summary: Handles message type 0x13 by decoding it and forwarding to FUN_004e0590.

results.name: network_message_handle_0x14
results.evidence: Requires role field == 0, decodes a group-3 packet into a 256-byte buffer, then calls FUN_004dff20; also reused for message type 0x25 by the dispatcher.
results.summary: Handles message types 0x14/0x25 by decoding a larger payload into a local buffer and forwarding it to FUN_004dff20.

results.name: network_message_handle_0x15
results.evidence: Requires role field == 0, decodes a group-3 packet, then calls FUN_004df090(0).
results.summary: Handles message type 0x15 by decoding it and scheduling a retry/notification via FUN_004df090.

results.name: network_message_handle_0x1a
results.evidence: Requires role field 0 or 1, decodes a group-5 packet, and if the sender's channel isn't yet established calls FUN_004e0bd0 (full info reply) or otherwise FUN_004dfc90.
results.summary: Handles message type 0x1a, sending a full server-info reply to not-yet-established machines or otherwise forwarding to FUN_004dfc90.

results.name: network_client_store_pending_game_data
results.evidence: Requires role field == 1 (client), decodes a group-5 packet into 8 dwords, and if flag byte +0x9f8 is clear and FUN_004de9f0 succeeds, copies the 32 bytes into fields at param_1+0x9d8 and sets +0x9f8.
results.summary: Client-side handler for message type 0x1b that latches an incoming 32-byte game/map data block into the client's pending-state fields.

results.name: network_message_handle_0x1c
results.evidence: Requires role field == 1, decodes a group-5 packet, then forwards the result to FUN_004df0e0.
results.summary: Client-side handler for message type 0x1c that decodes its payload and passes it to FUN_004df0e0.

results.name: network_message_handle_0x1d
results.evidence: Requires role field == 1, decodes a group-5 packet, then calls FUN_004df090(0).
results.summary: Client-side handler for message type 0x1d that decodes its payload and schedules a retry/notification via FUN_004df090.

results.name: network_message_handle_0x1e
results.evidence: Requires role field == 2, decodes a group-7 packet, then forwards the result to FUN_004df0e0.
results.summary: Handler restricted to role 2 for message type 0x1e that decodes its payload and passes it to FUN_004df0e0.

results.name: network_message_handle_0x23
results.evidence: Requires role field == 2, decodes a group-7 packet, then clears flag bit 2 on a field at unaff_ESI+0xe.
results.summary: Handler restricted to role 2 for message type 0x23 that decodes its payload and clears a status flag bit.

results.name: console_command_bool_get_set
results.evidence: cea-pdb hints match this to hs_inspect_boolean/hs_parse_boolean via the 'false' string; code prints '%s: %u' when argc==0 and otherwise parses argv[0] against '0'/'false'/'1'/'true' before storing into *unaff_EBX and re-printing -- used generically by sv_single_flag_force_reset.
results.summary: Shared console-command implementation that inspects or, given an argument, parses and sets a boolean value, then reports it -- used by boolean sv_* commands such as sv_single_flag_force_reset.

results.name: sv_map_reset
results.evidence: Strings 'sv_map_reset is a server-only function!', 'Map reset.', and 'Cannot restart the map when the game is over.' are printed directly by this function via chimera__console_out.
results.summary: Implements the sv_map_reset dedicated-server console command, restarting the current map if the game is not already ending.

results.name: sv_map
results.evidence: cea-pdb hint 'sv_map (game)' matches this function's strings ('sv_map is a server-only function!', 'sv_map specified invalid map or game variant') exactly; name already present and consistent with the code.
results.summary: Implements the sv_map console command: validates the requested map/variant and either starts a new dedicated-server game or restarts with the new variant.

results.name: network_scoreboard_find_next_player
results.evidence: Repeatedly calls data_iterator_next comparing each player datum's byte field at offset 0x67 (also used by network_channel_get_player_team) against unaff_ESI, but always returns 0xffffffff regardless of match, suggesting the real result is passed back through an unmodeled register.
results.summary: Iterates player data looking for an entry whose team/slot byte matches a caller value, used as a helper by the sv_players scoreboard printer.

results.name: sv_players
results.evidence: cea-pdb hint 'sv_players (game)' matches the string 'sv_players is a server-only function!' and the function prints a formatted player table with columns Number/Name/Score/TK Num/TK Timer via chimera__console_out.
results.summary: Implements the sv_players console command, printing a formatted scoreboard of connected players including score and team-kill statistics.

results.name: sv_players_scoreboard_row_loop
results.evidence: Body is essentially the tail loop of sv_players (0x4e2c70) -- same sprintf format string, same DAT_006f1d20/0087a480 lookups and formatting logic -- despite the pre-existing name implying an 'add player to game' hook, which the code does not support.
results.summary: Continuation of sv_players' row-formatting loop that prints each connected player's scoreboard line; the previously assigned add-player-hook name does not match the code's behavior.

results.name: sv_status
results.evidence: cea-pdb hint 'sv_status (game)' matches strings 'Dedicated server is running on map %s (%d / %d players)' and 'Game is ending...'; name already present and consistent with the code.
results.summary: Implements the sv_status console command, printing the current map, player count, and whether the game is ending.

results.name: sv_name
results.evidence: cea-pdb hint 'sv_name (networking)' matches strings 'sv_name: %ls' and the length/character-set validation messages; name already present and consistent with the code.
results.summary: Implements the sv_name console command, validating and setting the dedicated server's display name.

results.name: sv_password
results.evidence: cea-pdb hint 'sv_password (game)' matches strings 'sv_password: %ls' and the length/character-set validation messages; name already present and consistent with the code.
results.summary: Implements the sv_password console command, validating and setting the dedicated server's join password.

results.name: sv_single_flag_force_reset
results.evidence: Passes the literal string 'sv_single_flag_force_reset' as the command name into the generic boolean console-command handler (FUN_004e2990), saving and restoring DAT_0071c306 around the call.
results.summary: Implements the sv_single_flag_force_reset boolean console command using the shared get/set-boolean helper.

results.name: network_banlist_load
results.evidence: Opens a file via FUN_004e40a0/FUN_00624186, parses comma-separated 'name,hash,ban count,ban date' lines with _sscanf/_mktime, and populates entries through FUN_004e3890 -- the load counterpart to FUN_004e3380's '# Name, CD key hash, ban count, ban end date' writer.
results.summary: Loads the server's saved ban list from disk, parsing each player's name, CD-key hash, ban count, and ban-expiry date.

results.name: network_banlist_save
results.evidence: Writes the header '# Name, CD key hash, ban count, ban end date' and then one CSV-style line per entry from DAT_006b85a4[DAT_006b85a0], formatting the ban-expiry time with _localtime/__snprintf.
results.summary: Writes the current in-memory ban list out to disk in the CSV format read back by network_banlist_load.

results.name: sv_banlist
results.evidence: Prints a '[Num Bans Name]' header followed by '[%-4d %2d %*s]' rows built from the same DAT_006b85a4/DAT_006b85a0 ban table used by network_banlist_save/load, via chimera__console_out.
results.summary: Console command that lists the currently banned players with their ban counts.

results.name: network_banlist_add_ban
results.evidence: Looks up or creates a ban entry via FUN_004e3890, sets an indefinite or time-based expiry (FID_conflict___time32 + duration), prints 'Banning %s (%s) indefinitely.'/'...until %s %s.', and calls network_banlist_save to persist the change.
results.summary: Adds or extends a ban for a named player/hash for a given duration (or indefinitely) and saves the updated ban list.

results.name: network_session_autoban_player
results.evidence: Resolves a player-index parameter to a session machine slot, skips already-disconnecting machines, logs 'AUTOBAN: Banning %S.', then calls network_banlist_add_ban followed by FUN_004e0af0 to disconnect/kick the machine.
results.summary: Automatically bans and disconnects a given player, used by server-side auto-ban logic such as excessive team-killing.
